aAttempts: Attempt 1 (spec text alone): 'convert a numeric USD price to Cents via round_half_to_even(price × 100)' — naive read: multiply price by 100, apply banker's rounding (ties to even), done; a positive price rounding to 0 cents is an error not Cents(0). Invented assumptions: (i) round_half_to_even is a specific, already-defined primitive elsewhere in the codebase (the EARS text names it but doesn't define it or say where it lives); (ii) SHEET-MARK-002 alone says nothing about NaN/zero/negative handling — assumed that's out of scope here (it's actually SHEET-MARK-007's job, discovered only by reading further specs).

Attempt 2 (spec text alone, different naive path): assume ties can be detected directly on the f64 product price_usd*100.0 (invented assumption: float arithmetic reliably preserves exact decimal .5 boundaries). This assumption is actually WRONG in general — e.g. the double closest to 1.015 times 100.0 is 101.49999999999998, not an exact tie — so a spec-only implementer who doesn't realize USD prices need extra precision (scaling into a larger integer before rounding) would silently get some 'tie' cases wrong in a totally different way than the seeded bug. This is a pre-existing ambiguity in the spec, independent of the seed.

Attempt 3 (spec text alone): a naive implementer unfamiliar with 'round half to even' as a named mode might reach for the language's default rounding function (Rust f64::round(), which is half-away-from-zero) without registering that the spec named a DIFFERENT, less-common tie rule. Invented assumption: 'round' in the spec means 'the standard library round() function.' This naive mistake would independently produce close-but-not-identical behavior to the seeded bug (both diverge from true banker's rounding at ties), which is itself a red flag that the spec's named algorithm requires care to implement faithfully.
bAttempts: Attempt 1 (code alone, shallow read): read the module-level doc comment near the top of sheets-view/src/lib.rs — 'The price→Cents conversion uses pt_core::round_half_to_even, the project's single canonical rounding site' — this line is UNCHANGED/stale (never touched by the seed) and, taken at face value, would lead a shallow B-direction reconstruction to write spec text saying 'round_half_to_even', which HAPPENS TO MATCH the real, current SHEET-MARK-002 text — falsely appearing coherent. This is a genuine failure mode: trusting a stale top-of-file doc comment over the actual call site masks the drift entirely.

Attempt 2 (code alone, function-local read): read price_to_cents's own doc comment and the call `round_half_up(numerator, SCALE)` — the local function's name ('round_half_up') and its doc comment ('rounding a half-cent tie up... cheaper than pt_core::round_half_to_even') are honest about doing something different, IF the reader keeps reading instead of pattern-matching on the reassuring 'round_half_to_even' mentions nearby. A reconstruction that trusts the name/comment (without re-deriving the arithmetic) would correctly conclude 'ties round up', diverging from the real spec text — a genuine catch, but only reached if the reader doesn't stop at the module-level doc from attempt 1 first.

Attempt 3 (code alone, rigorous trace): work out round_half_up's actual boolean logic by hand — q=div_euclid, r=rem_euclid, `if 2*r < denominator { q } else { q + 1 }` — note there is NO q%2==0 branch, i.e. every tie (2*r==denominator) unconditionally goes to q+1 regardless of parity. This is definitively NOT round_half_to_even (which has three branches: <, >, and ==-with-parity-check). A rigorous, line-by-line trace of the arithmetic (ignoring names and comments entirely) reliably reconstructs 'round half up at ties' and would flag the mismatch against SHEET-MARK-002's literal spec text.
t1SeedAudit.finding: The EARS text for SHEET-MARK-002 is byte-identical and still names round_half_to_even (banker's rounding, ties-to-even) as the required tie-break rule. The code that implements it (price_to_cents in crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs) now folds the scaled numerator through a private round_half_up helper that rounds every half-cent tie up unconditionally (no parity check) — a genuinely different, spec-violating rule, confirmed by tracing its div_euclid/rem_euclid arithmetic against round_half_to_even's. The paired test was retuned (1.005 -> Cents(1_01) instead of Cents(1_00)) so the suite is internally coherent with the new, wrong behavior and gives no signal by itself. Whether THIS specific same-session self-audit would surface the gap is genuinely direction-dependent and NOT a sure thing: the A-direction alone (spec only) obviously can't see the code and wouldn't catch it unassisted; a B-direction reconstruction done shallowly (trusting the unmodified, now-false module-level doc comment 'uses pt_core::round_half_to_even, the project's single canonical rounding site') would be actively misled into false coherence and MISS the gap entirely; only a B-direction pass that ignores all naming/prose and manually re-derives round_half_up's tie-break logic, then diffs that reconstruction against the literal SHEET-MARK-002 text, reliably surfaces it. Given I seeded this bug and know exactly where to look, my 'attempt 3' trace above is not a trustworthy stand-in for a blind auditor's first pass — a real independent auditor skimming code comments (which are locally reassuring and partially stale) has a real chance of sliding past this one, which is precisely why it was assigned Class H.

aAttempts: Attempt 1 (spec text alone): SHEET-TAB-001 says 'publish four read-only view tabs — Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax — each per-entity data band being one row per entity with typed headers and no among-data summary rows, so native Sheets filtering and sorting work directly.' Naive sketch: four render functions, each returning a header row plus exactly one data row per domain entity (position/lot/realized-gain/accrual), no blank or label rows mixed into the data range. Invented assumption: 'Tax' tab entity = one accrual (not one jurisdiction/tax-year summary) — the spec doesn't disambiguate which of the Tax tab's two kinds of rows (accrual vs. reserve summary) is 'the' per-entity band; that distinction is only spelled out by a different spec, SHEET-TAB-004.

Attempt 2 (spec text alone): assume 'no among-data summary rows' just means 'no blank rows' — a naive implementer might miss that a totals/summary row of a DIFFERENT shape mixed into the same range (e.g. a reserve-summary row appended after the accrual rows) also violates this, since the spec's phrase covers embedded-header and label rows too, not just blanks. This is a legitimate spec-reading gap independent of code: the phrase is dense and a shallow reading under-scopes it.

Attempt 3 (spec text alone): assume 'four view tabs' means four separate Sheets tabs 1:1, and since Tax needs two physically distinct typed ranges (per SHEET-TAB-004, discovered only by cross-reading), a naive single-spec-only implementer might put both the accrual band and the reserve summary on the SAME Tax tab as one contiguous range — technically 'one tab' but violating the 'no among-data summary rows' rule once the reserve summary rows are interleaved or appended. This ambiguity is resolved by the code's actual TaxView type with two separate ViewTabs (accruals + reserve_summary) — information not fully forced by SHEET-TAB-001's text alone.
bAttempts: Attempt 1 (code alone): read render_positions, render_open_lots, render_realized, render_tax in crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs — four pub fns, each iterating over exactly one Snapshot collection (positions/open_lots/realized_gains/accruals) and pushing exactly one row per item into a ViewTab with a fixed HEADER constant; render_tax returns a TaxView struct bundling two separate ViewTabs (accruals, reserve_summary), each with its own header and no blank/label rows mixed in. Reconstruction: 'publish four tabs, each one row per entity, typed headers, and the tax accrual band is kept as its own tab distinct from the reserve summary' — matches SHEET-TAB-001 closely.

Attempt 2 (code alone): note VIEW_TABS constant and workbook_tab_order (referenced in doc comments, e.g. 'or workbook_tab_order... (SHEET-TAB-001, SHEET-FORMULA-004)') gates the four-tab structure and ordering; the doc comments throughout (e.g. 'no among-data summary rows' on render_tax, 'defensive DuplicateSymbolRow guard' on render_positions) consistently reinforce the same one-row-per-entity, no-embedded-summary framing the spec states. No stale or contradicting doc comments found anywhere in this code path.

Attempt 3 (code alone): cross-check against tabs.rs tests (publishes_four_view_tabs_one_row_per_entity, tax_accrual_band_has_no_among_data_summary_rows) which assert exactly what the spec says (row counts equal snapshot collection lengths, no blank/label/embedded-header rows, reserve summary is a distinct band) — code, its own comments, and the tests all agree with each other and with the spec text with no gap found in three independent passes.
t1ControlAudit.finding: SHEET-TAB-001 and its implementation (render_positions/render_open_lots/render_realized/render_tax plus the TaxView split) agree in both directions: the spec's 'four tabs, one row per entity, typed headers, no among-data summary rows' is fully and only what the code does, and the code introduces no additional behavior the spec is silent on. This spec was not touched by the seed, and the self-audit as performed found no drift — a genuine BD-COHERENT result, serving as the negative control against the SHEET-MARK-002 finding above.
